turn_text: Thursday was a busy day on the House Agriculture Committee, as I understand, reaching out to provide some additional data with regard to how cattle prices are established across the country and establishing a library from USDA.

Yeah, that's true. Dr. Johnson from South Dakota led that initiative on USDA published market data, basically helping to improve price discovery in the cattle market. So that was the gist of the Cattle Contract Library Act of 2021. It's not new. It's modeled after a, you know, a port contract library that's currently maintained by USDA. So the idea is not necessarily new, but this one would apply to the cattle industry. And so it really has to do with addressing that, helping address the spread between producer prices and what's being paid at the grocery store and then helping really a more transparent effort in terms of price discovery.
Does it solve the problem of price discovery in the cattle market or is this one step among many?

Well, I think this is one step among many. I mean, back in the old days, it was fairly simple. You take your cattle to the sale barn and that transaction was as transparent as it gets. And so in that sense, now we have different factors that come into play. And a lot of questions being asked when you see the prices being paid at the grocery store versus what the cattle producers are actually receiving at the farm gate and there's some questions about that spread. So this is just one of, I think, probably many ways to help address that. And then, quite frankly, I think You know, if you are long actuals, you probably need to think about being short futures. And that doesn't necessarily mean that you've got to go out and play the futures market. But it doesn't mean that probably you can employ risk management strategy that's ideally suited to your operation, whether that be a livestock operation or a row crop operation, whereby you can put some protection in place through options. Options are a fixed cost. You don't have to make margin calls. And when the markets move against you, then you're in a better position to benefit or to at least have some level of assurance that there's not going to be such an adverse effect that you wouldn't be protected. So I think there are a variety of tools that can be employed to help improve the price of every model and the cash flow of the producer.
